title: Why More Young People Are Facing Cancer Diagnoses
subtitle: New data confirms a worrying trend of early-onset cancer in adults under 50

summary.en: Recent reports show that cancer rates are rising among people under 50 in several countries. While cancer is still most common in older adults, this new trend is causing concern for health experts. Researchers are looking at changes in diet, lifestyle, and environmental factors to explain the shift. Although better testing helps find more cases, it does not explain the full increase. Scientists are now working to identify what environmental or lifestyle changes have driven this change since the 1990s.
summary.zh: 近期報告顯示，多國五十歲以下族群的癌症發生率正在上升。雖然癌症在老年人中仍最為常見，但這項新趨勢已引起健康專家的擔憂。研究人員正透過檢視飲食、生活型態與環境因素來解釋這種轉變。儘管更好的檢測技術有助於發現更多病例，但這並不能解釋全部的增長。科學家目前正致力於找出自一九九○年代以來，究竟是哪些環境或生活型態的改變導致了這種變化。

paragraphs.en: For many years, the medical community believed that cancer was primarily a disease of old age. However, a new report from The Guardian Health reveals that this trend is changing. Recent data shows that people under the age of 50 are now facing higher rates of cancer than previous generations did at the same age. This phenomenon, often called “early-onset cancer,” has become a major point of concern for health experts who once expected each new generation to live healthier lives than their parents.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，醫學界一直認為癌症主要是老年疾病。然而，一份來自《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）的最新報告顯示，這種趨勢正在改變。近期數據顯示，五十歲以下族群罹患癌症的比率，已高於過去同齡的世代。這種現象通常被稱為「早發性癌症」，已成為健康專家的一大隱憂，因為他們原本預期每一代新人都會比父母活得更健康。

paragraphs.en: This update follows recent research highlighting that cancer rates are rising faster among younger populations in countries such as England, the US, and the Netherlands. While experts previously noted that cancer is still most common in older adults, the consistent rise in younger people is difficult to ignore. The World Cancer Research Fund studied 12 different types of cancer over the last 20 years to understand this shift. Their findings show that for women under 50, cancers of the breast, bowel, and liver are increasing. Similar patterns were observed in men, with higher numbers of bowel, kidney, and prostate cancer cases reported.
paragraphs.zh: 這項更新研究凸顯了英國、美國與荷蘭等國家的年輕族群癌症發生率正快速上升。儘管專家先前指出癌症在老年人中仍最為常見，但年輕族群中持續上升的趨勢已不容忽視。世界癌症研究基金會（World Cancer Research Fund）在過去二十年間研究了十二種不同類型的癌症，以了解這種轉變。研究結果顯示，五十歲以下的女性中，乳癌、腸癌與肝癌的病例正在增加；男性也觀察到類似模式，腸癌、腎臟癌與攝護腺癌的病例數皆有所上升。

paragraphs.en: One common question is whether these higher numbers are simply the result of better medical technology. According to The Guardian Health, while modern diagnostic tools — machines and tests used to find diseases — do help doctors identify more cases, they do not explain the entire increase. The data indicates that younger people are truly experiencing a higher incidence of these diseases compared to their parents when they were the same age. This means the problem is not just that we are looking harder for cancer, but that more people are actually developing it.
paragraphs.zh: 一個常見的疑問是，這些數字的增加是否僅僅是因為醫療技術進步所致。根據《衛報健康》報導，雖然現代診斷工具（即用於發現疾病的機器與檢測）確實協助醫師識別出更多病例，但這並不能解釋整體的增長。數據顯示，與父母同齡時相比，年輕人確實面臨更高的疾病發生率。這意味著問題不僅在於我們更努力篩檢癌症，而是實際上罹患癌症的人數確實變多了。

paragraphs.en: Scientists are now working to identify what has changed in the environment and our daily lives since the 1990s. One major area of focus is diet. Over the past 50 years, there has been a significant rise in the consumption of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks. These dietary changes are closely linked to rising obesity rates. Globally, obesity among adolescents has quadrupled since 1990. Excess body fat is a known risk factor for chronic inflammation and metabolic dysfunction, which can make the body more likely to develop cancer.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家目前正致力於找出自一九九○年代以來，環境與日常生活發生了哪些改變。飲食是主要的關注領域之一。過去五十年間，超加工食品與含糖飲料的攝取量顯著增加。這些飲食習慣的改變與肥胖率上升密切相關。全球青少年肥胖率自一九九○年以來已成長為原先的四倍。體內脂肪過多是導致慢性發炎與代謝功能障礙的已知風險因子，這會使身體更容易罹患癌症。

paragraphs.en: However, diet and weight alone do not tell the whole story. The Guardian Health noted that for some conditions, such as breast cancer in women before menopause, the link to body weight is complex and sometimes contradictory. Because of this, researchers are also investigating the impact of environmental toxins. These include chemicals, plastics, and pollution in the air and water that have become common in our daily lives. Identifying a single cause is difficult because cancer can develop many years after a person is exposed to a harmful substance. Furthermore, people are exposed to a wide range of different pollutants throughout their lives, making it hard for scientists to point to one specific factor.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，飲食與體重並不能解釋所有問題。《衛報健康》指出，對於某些病症，例如女性停經前的乳癌，其與體重的關聯相當複雜，有時甚至相互矛盾。因此，研究人員也正在調查環境毒素的影響。這些毒素包括在日常生活中已變得司空見慣的化學物質、塑膠與空氣及水中的汙染物。要找出單一成因相當困難，因為癌症可能在人體接觸有害物質多年後才發病。此外，人們一生中會接觸到各式各樣的汙染物，這使得科學家難以指出某個特定的因素。

paragraphs.en: This health trend comes at a time when global guidelines are also shifting regarding other health issues. For example, recent advice has warned against using weight-loss drugs for children under ten, suggesting that families should focus on healthy eating and exercise instead. This focus on lifestyle reflects a broader effort to address the root causes of health problems in younger populations. As obesity rates continue to climb, the pressure to find effective public health solutions is growing.
paragraphs.zh: 這項健康趨勢出現的同時，全球對於其他健康議題的準則也在轉變。例如，近期的建議警告不應讓十歲以下兒童使用減肥藥物，並建議家庭應將重點放在健康飲食與運動上。這種對生活型態的重視，反映出各界正努力解決年輕族群健康問題的根本原因。隨著肥胖率持續攀升，尋求有效公共衛生解決方案的壓力也日益增加。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the medical community faces a difficult challenge. Scientists must continue to study the long-term effects of modern life on human health. While the rise in early-onset cancer is alarming, understanding the specific environmental and lifestyle triggers is the first step toward prevention. For now, experts emphasize that while the situation is serious, ongoing research is essential to protect future generations. The goal remains to move back toward a future where younger people can expect to live longer, healthier lives than those who came before them.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，醫學界正面臨一項艱鉅的挑戰。科學家必須持續研究現代生活對人類健康的長期影響。雖然早發性癌症的增加令人擔憂，但了解特定的環境與生活型態誘發因子，是預防的第一步。目前，專家強調儘管情況嚴峻，持續的研究對於保護未來世代至關重要。目標依然是回歸到一個年輕人能預期比前人活得更長壽、更健康的未來。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A specific issue or subject that causes worry or requires attention.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 令人擔憂的重點；關注點。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語由多個常見字組成，但合起來指「令人擔憂的議題」。文中：This phenomenon, often called “early-onset cancer,” has become a major point of concern for health experts who once expected each new generation to live healthier lives than their parents.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To provide all the facts or the complete explanation for a situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 說明事情的全部真相；解釋完整的情況。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「講完整個故事」，實際用於表示某個因素不足以解釋全貌。文中：However, diet and weight alone do not tell the whole story.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To identify or indicate a specific cause or factor.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「用手指著某物」，這裡引申為「找出導致某事的關鍵因素」。文中：Furthermore, people are exposed to a wide range of different pollutants throughout their lives, making it hard for scientists to point to one specific factor.

quiz.question: According to the findings from the World Cancer Research Fund, which of the following is true regarding gender-specific cancer trends in people under 50?

options.A: Men are experiencing a higher incidence of breast cancer than women.
options.B: Bowel cancer is a shared concern for both men and women in this age group.
options.C: Liver cancer is the most common form of cancer for both genders.
options.D: Prostate cancer is now the leading cause of death for men under 50.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，研究指出女性有乳腺癌、腸癌和肝癌的增加，而男性則有腸癌、腎癌和前列腺癌的增加，因此「腸癌（bowel cancer）」是兩者共同提到的項目。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及男性罹患乳腺癌；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章僅提到肝癌是女性增加的癌症之一，並非兩性共同最常見；選項 D 錯誤，文章僅提到前列腺癌病例增加，並未將其定義為該年齡層男性死亡的主因。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the role of modern medical technology in the rising rates of early-onset cancer?

options.A: It is the primary reason why younger people are getting sicker.
options.B: It has failed to detect any new cases of cancer in younger populations.
options.C: It contributes to identifying more cases, but does not account for the entire increase.
options.D: It has become less effective at identifying diseases compared to the 1990s.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段，作者提到現代診斷工具確實幫助醫生發現更多病例，但數據顯示這並不能解釋所有增長，這意味著實際罹病率確實上升了。選項 A 與文章觀點相反；選項 B 錯誤，因為技術確實有助於診斷；選項 D 錯誤，文章並未提到技術效率下降，反而是強調技術進步但仍無法完全解釋病例激增的現象。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'chronic' mean as used in the phrase 'chronic inflammation'?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在醫學語境中，「chronic（慢性的）」指的是長期存在或持續不斷的狀態。文章提到肥胖導致的身體發炎反應，通常是指長期累積的健康問題。選項 A 與「acute（急性的）」定義混淆；選項 C 雖然慢性病可能伴隨疼痛，但並非該詞的核心定義；選項 D 錯誤，慢性病通常難以快速治癒，且與該詞定義無直接關聯。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding early-onset cancer?

options.A: Cancer rates in younger people are rising, and researchers are investigating complex lifestyle and environmental factors.
options.B: The rise in cancer among young people is entirely due to the consumption of ultra-processed foods.
options.C: Medical technology has improved enough to eliminate the threat of cancer for future generations.
options.D: Environmental toxins are the only proven cause of the increase in cancer cases among the youth.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章整體主旨是探討年輕族群癌症率上升的警訊，並說明科學家正從飲食、肥胖及環境毒素等多方面進行研究，尋找根本原因。選項 B 太過絕對，文章提到飲食僅是因素之一；選項 C 錯誤，文章強調這仍是嚴峻挑戰，並未宣稱威脅已被消除；選項 D 錯誤，文章明確指出原因複雜，包含飲食、肥胖與環境等多種因素，而非單一原因。
